theme: Healing at the gate; preaching; opposition begins
readingInstruction: Read Acts 3:1-4:31. Peter and John heal a lame man at the temple gate, Peter preaches, and the apostles are arrested. They answer the council with bold words, and the church prays for boldness. Notice how Peter ties everything to Jesus’ name.
settingTheScene: Peter and John go up to the temple at the hour of prayer, three in the afternoon. At the Beautiful Gate, a man lame from birth is carried every day to beg. What follows is the first public miracle in Acts, and it leads to the first conflict with the authorities. The same leaders who condemned Jesus now face his disciples.
observation: “I have no silver and gold, but what I do have I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!” (3:6).
“And you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead” (3:15).
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out” (3:19).
“You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, And in your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed” (3:25).
“And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved” (4:12).
“Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were uneducated, common men, they were astonished. And they recognized that they had been with Jesus” (4:13).
“For we cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard” (4:20).
“And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness” (4:31).
interpretation:
The lame man expects money. Peter says, “I have no silver and gold, but what I do have I give to you.” What the church has is far greater: the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. The man leaps up and enters the temple walking and leaping and praising God. The crowd gathers in amazement, and Peter preaches.

His sermon makes three points. First, don’t look at us; the power is Jesus’. God has glorified his servant Jesus, whom you denied and killed, the Author of life, whom God raised. Second, you acted in ignorance, but God used it to fulfill what the prophets said about the Christ’s suffering. Third, repent and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out, that times of refreshing may come from the Lord. And he reminds them that they are heirs of the covenant with Abraham: in your offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed. God raised up his servant and sent him to you first, to bless you by turning every one of you from your wickedness. The Abrahamic promise is the framework for the mission.

The priests and the captain of the temple guard arrest them. But many who heard believed, and the number of men grew to about five thousand. The next day, before the same council that condemned Jesus, Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks of the rejected stone (Psalm 118): “There is salvation in no other name.” This is a bold claim of Jesus’ exclusivity. The council marvels at the confidence of “uneducated, common men” and recognizes that they had been with Jesus. With the healed man standing beside them, they have nothing to say. They warn them to stop speaking in this name. Peter and John answer: “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge, for we cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard.”

When released, they go to their friends, and the whole church prays. They do not ask for safety. They quote Psalm 2 (which you read in a few days) and pray for boldness. The place is shaken, and they are all filled with the Spirit and speak the word of God with boldness.
connection: Isaiah 52:13 and 53:11 speak of God’s servant. Deuteronomy 18:15 is the prophet like Moses. Genesis 12:3 and 22:18 are the Abrahamic promise. Psalm 118:22 is the stone. Psalm 2:1-2 is quoted in Acts 4:25-26. Philippians 2:9-11 says God gave him the name above every name. John 14:6 says no one comes to the Father except through him. Hebrews 13:15 calls us to continually offer a sacrifice of praise.
application:
Ask what you have to give that is better than silver and gold. Give it to someone this week.

When you are afraid to speak about Jesus, pray the church’s prayer: not for safety, but for boldness.

Let people take note that you have been with Jesus. How?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that there is no other name by which we must be saved.
Ask him to make you bold.
Tell him what you would say to someone about him today.
